candidates.label: Neapolis archaeological remains (Kavala)
candidates.support: This Neapolis, the seaport of Philippi in Macedonia and continuous with modern Kavala, is a distinct place from Neapolis in Samaria (Flavia Neapolis, modern Nablus) and from other ancient cities named Neapolis. The Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire's coordinate for the site and Wikidata's coordinate for Kavala agree closely.

summary.text: Neapolis was, per Pleiades, on the coast of Thrace, and served as the port of Philippi in Hellenistic and Roman times. Acts records the route by which Paul's party reached it: from Troas by way of Samothrace to Neapolis, and from there to Philippi.

scripture.textWEB: Setting sail therefore from Troas, we made a straight course to Samothrace, and the day following to Neapolis;
